numbered_critiques.concern: Rename-only commits are structurally invisible to the lint, yet the edge-case inventory lists that case under *Handled*. On the tree's only supersession, the entire commit enumerates as a single rename into `archive/`; a rename is never a trigger and the destination is excluded by the `/archive/` substring rule, so the commit never reaches a claim check at all. The inventory spends a paragraph arguing such a commit does append a `## Decision` section — but under the proposal's own trigger rule the commit is never examined, so whether it appends a section is irrelevant. Consequently the shape-(a) vocabulary's `reject` and `supersede` tokens can never be evaluated on the only commit shape doctrine assigns them: they are dead tokens in v1. The same holds for every plan-archive commit. The general rule — 'a commit whose only lifecycle-file motion is a rename is invisible' — is stated nowhere, yet it silently exempts an entire class. 'Handled' reads as 'checked and correct'; the truth is 'silently exempt', and presenting silent exemption as coverage is precisely the overclaim this repo kills proposals for (the same class of error the sibling's R9 flagged).
numbered_critiques.grounding: `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -M -r b064576` emits exactly one line: `R091	dev/proposals/2026-07-08-claude-automated-review-committer.md	dev/proposals/archive/...` — zero A/M entries under a trigger root, so not examined. Same for `d789414` (only `M dev/PLANNING.md` + `R091` plan->archive). Independent prototype confirms neither commit is triggered. Doctrine: `doctrine/proposals.md:322-325` — '**Rejected** and **superseded** proposals move to `dev/proposals/archive/` in the Decision commit itself.'
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Move the reject/supersede-plus-archive case from *Handled* to *Known omissions*, quoting the b064576 enumeration as proof, and state the general rule explicitly: 'a commit whose only lifecycle-file motion is a rename (proposal->archive, plan->archive) is never examined; reject/supersede Decisions and plan-archives are therefore outside coverage.' Add `b064576` and `d789414` to the corpus test as must-SKIP (not merely must-not-flag) so the gap is pinned rather than latent. Either drop `reject`/`supersede` from the claim vocabulary or mark them explicitly as dead tokens in v1.

numbered_critiques.concern: Three load-bearing matcher details are unpinned or wrong inside the one section that declares 'Everything below is pinned here, not deferred to the plan.' (a) CASE-SENSITIVITY: the claim regex is given as `(?<![-\w])<token>s?(?![-\w])` over an all-lowercase token vocabulary, with no mention of `re.IGNORECASE`. Every real subject in the corpus capitalizes. Under a literal reading of the pinned spec, f4a8308 yields no claim and therefore no shape-(a) finding — directly contradicting the headline result ('3 findings ... f4a8308 once (shape (a))') and reddening the corpus-regression test on the day it lands. The dogfood cannot disambiguate this, because a case-sensitive build produces zero false positives too — it just produces silent false negatives that look like passes. (b) `-M` THRESHOLD: `-M` is argued entirely on its upside ('load-bearing and this is verified') with no examination of the failure mode it introduces. Empirically it changes the *trigger set* on 0 of 120 commits — the `/archive/` exclusion already defuses every real case, and the 'general case' it is defended by (a slug-correction rename within `dev/proposals/`) has never occurred. Meanwhile bare `-M` is a global similarity heuristic that can convert a genuine `A` into an `R` and silently un-trigger a commit; Cairn plans are derived from their proposals, which makes this concrete rather than theoretical. (c) `open`/`opening` TOKENS: the `open` claim fires on any bare 'open' in the subject and requires an `A` entry as evidence, so an M-only commit whose subject merely mentions Cairn's own live 'Open questions' vocabulary is a false positive. Today's rate is 0 only because every historical use of 'open' happens to be a transition verb — the precision rests on an undocumented subject-line convention (`dev/<tree>: open <slug>`), not on the rule. The `opening` token is pure downside: zero true positives in 536 subjects.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) `git log -1 --format='%s' f4a8308` -> 'dev/proposals: add Gemini External Review for check_cairn self-host-compat'; `git log -1 --format='%h %s' f0ce2af` -> 'Maintainer Decision -- ACCEPT record-corrections'; `git log -1 --format='%h %s' 2306f07` -> 'dev/proposals: record-corrections -- Response + Revised'. (b) `-r` vs `-M -r` trigger sets compared across all 120 commits: zero differences. `git log --diff-filter=R -M -- 'dev/proposals/*'` returns 5 renames, all proposal->archive; no slug correction exists. Synthetic repo demo: a plan-open adding `dev/plans/a-thing.md` derived from its proposal and deleting the proposal without archiving reports `A`+`D` under `-r` but `R096 dev/proposals/2026-01-01-a-thing.md -> dev/plans/a-thing.md` under `-M`. Cairn plans are proposal-derived — `dev/plans/archive/review-record-integrity.md:15` (`## Source proposal`). (c) 12 of 536 subjects match the open vocabulary and all 12 are genuine opens (regex over `git log --format=%s`); none uses 'opening'. 'Open questions' is live vocabulary: `dev/proposals/2026-07-11-claude-record-corrections.md:248`, `:482`, `:541`, and `templates/core/dev/strategy/_template.md:129`. Running the proposal's matcher: 'dev/proposals: transition-lint -- resolve open questions from the Internal review' -> claim=open; 'dev/plans: X -- close out the open acceptance criteria' -> claim=open; 'dev/plans: transition-lint -- opening sequence step 1' -> claim=open. numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: (a) State case-insensitive matching explicitly in the pinned spec (`re.IGNORECASE`, or the flag inline), and add a synthetic-tier test asserting that an all-lowercase and an all-uppercase subject produce the same finding. (b) Pin the similarity threshold explicitly — `--find-renames=100%` (or `=90%`) rather than bare `-M` — so pairing is near-exact and a derived plan cannot be absorbed into a rename; add the synthetic derived-plan commit as a must-flag/must-trigger test; and record that `-M` currently changes the trigger set on 0/120 real commits so its cost/benefit is stated honestly. (c) Drop the `opening` token. Anchor the `open` token positionally — require it to be the first word after the `dev/<tree>: ` prefix (which all 12 true positives satisfy) — or require it be immediately followed by a slug-like token. Add the three subjects above as must-not-flag synthetic tests so the regression is pinned.

numbered_critiques.concern: The exit-code contract has a silent-clean hole, and it cites one git precedent while adopting the opposite error posture from another. The proposal names `scripts/measurements.py:24-27`, `:51`, `:139` as its safe-git precedent — but `measurements.py:150-153` runs git with `check=True` and RAISES on failure, while the design adopts `templates/modules/team-gated/_intent/conflict.py:757-758`'s 'empty on any git error, degrade to prior behaviour'. Combined with 'the only non-zero return is 2, for ... an *unparsable* rev-range', a range that passes the regex but does not RESOLVE (`deadbeef..HEAD`, a deleted branch name, a typo'd SHA) enumerates nothing, prints nothing, and exits 0 — indistinguishable from a clean scan. For a tool whose entire value proposition is 'I ran it and saw nothing,' that is the one failure mode that must never be silent, and it is not covered by the edge-case inventory (which lists only 'empty rev-range (no findings, exit 0)').
numbered_critiques.grounding: scripts/measurements.py:150-153 (`check=True`) vs templates/modules/team-gated/_intent/conflict.py:757-758 and :759-767 (`check=False`, return {} on rc!=0); the proposal's own 'Exit behaviour' and 'Edge-case inventory' sections.

Always print a one-line census — `scanned N commits, T triggered, F findings` — so a zero-finding run is positive evidence rather than silence. State which of the two git-error postures applies where.

numbered_critiques.concern: Both halves of the human-facing signal are uninformative as specified. Verified: `git rev-parse --short HEAD~20` = `755165d`, and `17b7e5c` is NOT in `HEAD~20..HEAD`; the proposal's own table records ZERO findings over the last 45 commits. So the DEFAULT invocation returns nothing, indefinitely, for as long as the discipline holds. Meanwhile the only documented invocation that shows anything (`d6646a3..HEAD`) reports the same two immutable historical commits every single run — and the proposal explicitly refuses to whitelist them ('the two historical incident commits must keep flagging, since they are the acid test'). Since history is immutable, that is a permanent, unfixable 3-line wall on the one command a Maintainer is told to run: precisely the 'trains people to ignore it' Theme-3.4 failure the proposal elsewhere guards against, arriving on day one rather than after drift.

numbered_critiques.concern: The pre-registered R10 constraint named three suppression layers; the design ships two and drops the only one that scales. `dev/proposals/archive/2026-07-08-claude-review-record-integrity.md:375-378` says the R6/Theme-3.4 lesson is the suppression infrastructure — 'exclusion roots + whitelist + info downgrade' — and the accepted Response at `:479-481` pins 'the info-tier analogy' as carried into Part C. The consequence is concrete: `scripts/quality_gate.py:634` (`sev = "info" if name.startswith("_") else "fail"`) is a CLASS-level downgrade, which is what R6 actually needed; transition_lint has no equivalent. A recurring false-positive SHAPE (a new commit-subject convention) can then only be absorbed one SHA at a time, forever — which the proposal's own Signals section half-notices ('if entries accumulate past a handful, retire the tool'). numbered_critiques.concern: The lint detects over-claiming only, never bundling — which is the other half of the very rule it quotes as its warrant. `doctrine/lifecycle.md:28-30` prohibits *bundling* (one commit carrying two transitions), and `doctrine/proposals.md:85-87` carries two clauses; the proposal quotes both but the heuristics test only 'message claims a transition the diff lacks.' Nothing checks the converse: a diff carrying lifecycle work the message does not announce, or lifecycle work bundled with implementation work. Worse, 'a subject claims at most one transition' (leftmost-wins) means an honest bundler is checked on its first claim only, so the tool is guaranteed blind to the very shape the rule exists to prevent; shape (b) covers exactly one bundling pair (open + baked-in review). This is defensible as a v1 scope bound, but it is not in the *Explicit non-goals* list, so the Rationale's claim that the tool 'makes an existing rule mechanically visible' reads as broader coverage than the design delivers.

It does not detect the converse — unannounced lifecycle work, or lifecycle work bundled with implementation work (the second clause of `doctrine/proposals.md:85-87`).' Soften the Rationale from 'makes an existing rule mechanically visible' to naming the corner actually covered (over-claiming, plus the open + baked-in-review bundling pair). Optionally add a cheap symmetric check — flag when two or more distinct evidence sections each receive >=3 added non-blank lines in one commit.
